question: In a Cartesian coordinate system in the plane, point \(P(4,3)\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise about point \(C(1,1)\) to obtain point \(P'\). Find the coordinates of \(P'\) (enter the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma).
solution:
Relative to \(C(1,1)\), \(P(4,3)\) is \(4-1=3\) units right and \(3-1=2\) units up. A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation turns a rightward step upward and an upward step leftward, preserving their lengths. Thus \(P'\) is \(2\) units left and \(3\) units up from \(C\), giving
\[
P'=(1-2,\,1+3)=(-1,4).
\]
